title: Dancing before the ark (2 Samuel 6)
hook: David dances with all his might and his wife despises him

segments.voice: Yesterday, the cave, and a hem cut from a king's robe instead of his life. Your line was I will not.

Saul is gone now, and David is king in Jerusalem. He sets out to bring the ark of God into his city: the gold-covered chest that held the tablets of the law, the place Israel knew as God's throne among them. The first attempt goes badly. The ark rides on a new cart, the oxen stumble, a man named Uzzah reaches out to steady it, and he dies on the spot. David is shaken. How shall the ark of the Lord come to me? he asks. He leaves it at the house of a man named Obed-edom, and it stays there three months.
screen: `DAVID WANTS THE ARK IN JERUSALEM.` → `THE OXEN STUMBLE.` → `HOW SHALL THE ARK COME TO ME?`

segments.voice: Then word comes that God has blessed Obed-edom's whole household because of the ark. So David tries again, this time with joy. After six steps he offers a sacrifice. Trumpets, shouting, the whole city in the street. And the king, the Douay-Rheims says, "danced with all his might before the Lord." Not a dignified sway. Leaping, whirling, dressed only in a simple linen ephod, a priest's garment, not his royal robes. Up at a window, someone is watching: Michal, David's wife, Saul's daughter. And she "despised him in her heart." When he comes home she lets him have it: how glorious the king of Israel was today, uncovering himself in front of the servant girls like some fool. David's answer is the heart of the story. It was before the Lord, he says, and "I will be little in my own eyes." He'll look foolish again if that's what praise costs. Catholics read this chapter beside a second story. In Luke's Gospel, Mary travels to the hill country of Judah to visit her cousin Elizabeth. Elizabeth cries out, why should the mother of my Lord come to me? It echoes David's question about the ark. The baby John leaps in Elizabeth's womb, the way David leapt before the ark. And Mary stays three months, as the ark stayed three months in that house. Catholic tradition draws these threads together and calls Mary the Ark of the Covenant, the one who carried God's presence. You'll hear that title in the Litany of Loreto.
screen: `DANCING WITH ALL HIS MIGHT.` · `MICHAL DESPISED HIM IN HER HEART.` · `LITTLE IN MY OWN EYES.` · `MARY, THE ARK OF THE COVENANT.` · then, large: `DAVID DANCED WITH ALL HIS MIGHT.`

segments.voice: Picture something you're grateful for, really grateful, and let your body show it a little: lift your hands, smile with your whole face, sway, with nobody grading. If you pray, offer that joy to God the way David did; if you don't, let yourself be glad without checking who's at the window.
ark. The chest carrying God's presence, which David danced before with all his might, saying, I will be little in my own eyes. Today's word.
Your line: dance anyway. Little in your own eyes, and glad. That's day four hundred four.

howItsDone: In the Litany of Loreto, Catholics call on Mary as Ark of the Covenant, and the Vigil Mass of the Assumption reads the Chronicles account of David bringing the ark into Jerusalem.

fork.setup: you're David. the ark is finally coming into your city, the trumpets are sounding, and the whole crowd is watching their king. what do you do?
options: walk beside it with royal dignity.
dance before the Lord with all your might.
fork.reveal: he dances with all his might in a linen ephod. Michal despises him for it, and he says: I will be little in my own eyes.

original.note: Hebrew: chest, ark. The ark of the covenant held the tablets of the law; the Church gives the title to Mary.

trapdoor: what you thought: a king who liked to dance.
what it means: David drops every bit of royal dignity for joy before God's presence, and won't apologize for looking small.
what a scholar hears: Luke's Visitation echoes this chapter: a question like David's, a leap before God's presence, three months in a house. hence Mary, Ark of the Covenant.

chat.says: Why do Catholics call Mary the Ark of the Covenant?
options: Like the ark, she carried God's presence; Luke echoes David's story.
Because she kept the tablets of the law safe in her home.
Because she was born in the town where the ark was kept.
chat.meaning: Elizabeth's question, John's leap and Mary's three months echo David and the ark; tradition calls Mary the one who carried God's presence.

Uzzah.meaning: the man who reached out to steady the ark and died

Obed-edom.meaning: the man whose house kept the ark three months

ephod.meaning: a simple linen garment worn by priests

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): cut 'the first great thing he wants to do' (not in the text); 'and it's beautiful' (empty uplift) removed; unsourced 'early Christian writers noticed' made 'Catholic tradition draws these threads together'; howItsDone now names the Chronicles reading at the Assumption vigil.

The Ark–Visitation parallels (2 Samuel 6:9 / Luke 1:43; leaping; three months, 6:11 / Luke 1:56) are a common Catholic typology; 'early Christian writers noticed' is general. Confirm attribution (e.g. Ambrose, Athanasius are often cited).
howItsDone: the Vigil Mass of the Assumption uses 1 Chronicles 15–16 (David bringing the ark into the tent), not 2 Samuel 6. Confirm wording 'pair David bringing the ark into Jerusalem'.
The Douay renders Michal's rebuke as uncovering himself 'as if one of the buffoons should be naked'; paraphrased gently as 'like some fool'.
